reason: The text mentions only three named entities: Moses (מֹשֶׁה), Aaron (אַהֲרֹן), and God (יְהוָה). Moses is explicitly the leader who directs the Levites and receives divine instruction. Aaron, mentioned in the context of his role regarding the people, is the high priest and brother of Moses, also serving as a leader. All other persons mentioned ('the people,' 'the sons of Levi,' 'men') are referred to generically without individual names. While God might not be classified as a human 'character' per se, God functions as the ultimate authority in the passage and could be considered the supreme leader. Thus, every individually named entity in the passage holds a leadership position.
